Side slope and green contour. Rhys pointed out that the fairways went up and down but were level from side to side, and the greens were interesting only in outline. Measured on round 2: fairways leaned 0–0.8% across, three greens were dead flat, three were a single 1–1.5% plane, and only the 2nd had a tier. New standing rules for every course (docs/COURSE-DESIGN.md, "Side slope and green contour"), applied here first.

Every par 4 and 5 now leans where drives land, each one for a reason. 1st: 3% left, toward the forest, so the right half by the bunker is the place to be. 2nd: 3% right, down the gully. 6th: 2–3% toward the terrace edge, kicking a drive toward the corner. 8th: 4–5% left at the crest, away from the lake. 9th: 2–3% left along the shore, away from the lava.

Two strong sidehills. The 4th's lay-up past the bridge runs along the cone's flank and leans 6–7% left, so the third is played with the ball above your feet (the approach bunker on the left catches what runs). The 7th's ledge leans 6.5% back toward the wall, the way a slumped block tilts as it slides, away from the 18 m drop on the right.

Greens: moderate, like a modern course. Each falls about 1.5–2% underfoot. Seven of nine also have a feature: the 1st and 8th a shallow bowl in the back lobe that gathers to a back pin; the 2nd and 9th a tier at the back (0.5 and 0.4 m); the 5th a swale down the middle that gathers from both horns; the 6th the bold one, the back of the bar 0.6 m up on a tier; the 7th a low spine walling off the wing. The 3rd (the punchbowl) and the 4th (the false front) stay flatter: their surrounds are the feature.

New on each hole page: the green. A diagram with 5 cm contours, arrows pointing downhill (red where it's steeper than 3%) and the pin areas as dashed rings, drawn with the approach coming up from the bottom. The text adds a contour line: typical slope, how much shape there is beyond the fall, pin areas, cuppable share, and the fairway's lean at each target.

Measured, not eyeballed. The checks (out/grid/checks.txt) now report each landing area's lean and each green's slope, shape, pin and pin areas, with a warning when fewer than half the par 4/5s lean 2% or more, when there isn't one or two strong ones, or when fewer than five greens have a feature. All pass: 7 of 7 lean, 2 strong, 7 greens with a feature. Every pin is at 3% or less. The narrow greens (2, 5, 6, 8, 9) have two pin areas each, the rest three.
Unchanged: the routing, every green's outline, the bunkers, the tees and all of round 2's lava.
